pharm: Bactericidal beta-lactam that binds penicillin-binding proteins to inhibit bacterial cell-wall synthesis; broad gram-negative (including Pseudomonas) and gram-positive coverage with stability against many beta-lactamases.
quick: 1-2 g IV every 8-12 h depending on infection
Use if clearly needed; limited human data
Excreted in milk in low amounts; generally compatible
Reduce dose/frequency by CrCl; major adjustment needed
Renal function, neurologic status, signs of superinfection
summary: Cefepime is a fourth-generation cephalosporin given intravenously (or intramuscularly for selected UTIs) for pneumonia, febrile neutropenia, complicated urinary and intra-abdominal infections, and skin/skin-structure infections caused by susceptible organisms. It has broad gram-negative coverage including Pseudomonas aeruginosa. It is renally eliminated and must be dose-adjusted in renal impairment, where accumulation can cause neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus).
indications: Empiric therapy for febrile neutropenic patients
Uncomplicated and complicated urinary tract infections, including pyelonephritis
Complicated intra-abdominal infections (in combination with metronidazole)

dosage.n: Use 2 g IV every 8 h if Pseudomonas aeruginosa
IM route only for mild/moderate UTI due to E. coli

dosage.d: 2 g IV every 12 hours (intra-abdominal: every 8-12 h with metronidazole)
dosage.n: Pair with metronidazole for intra-abdominal infection

dosage.d: Reduce dose/interval per CrCl (e.g., usual dose every 24 h at CrCl 11-29; further reduce <11)
dosage.n: Supplement after hemodialysis; pediatric dosing 50 mg/kg per dose

admin: Administer by IV infusion over approximately 30 minutes (preferred route)
Reconstitute and dilute per labeling; inspect for particulates and discoloration
Reserve IM route for mild/moderate UTI due to E. coli
Adjust dose by creatinine clearance to avoid neurotoxic accumulation
moa: Cefepime is a bactericidal cephalosporin that binds to penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and inhibits the final transpeptidation step of peptidoglycan cell-wall synthesis, leading to cell lysis. It rapidly penetrates gram-negative bacteria and is highly stable to hydrolysis by many chromosomal and plasmid-mediated beta-lactamases, giving it broad-spectrum activity including against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

absolute: Immediate hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis) to cefepime or other cephalosporins, penicillins, or other beta-lactams
monitor: Renal function and dose appropriateness for CrCl

preg: Available human data are limited; animal studies have not shown harm. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Cefepime is excreted into human milk in low concentrations; it is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding, though the infant may be monitored for diarrhea or thrush.
renal: Cefepime is primarily eliminated by the kidneys; dosage and/or interval must be reduced in renal impairment. Accumulation in unadjusted renal failure causes neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, aphasia, myoclonus, seizures, and nonconvulsive status epilepticus). Supplemental dosing is needed after hemodialysis.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

major: Potent diuretics (e.g., furosemide) - potential additive nephrotoxicity
moderate: Probenecid (may reduce renal clearance of cephalosporins)
minor: Live typhoid vaccine (antibacterials may reduce response)
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive urine glucose test with copper-reduction methods; positive direct Coombs test has been reported.

serious: Neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus)

monitoring: Neurologic status, especially in renal impairment
Signs of allergic reaction and superinfection
counsel: This antibiotic is given by injection or infusion, usually in hospital
Report any rash, itching, swelling, or difficulty breathing immediately
Tell staff if you become confused, twitchy, or have a seizure
Report severe or watery/bloody diarrhea, which can occur even after stopping the drug
pk: End of IV infusion (~0.5 h); ~1.4-1.6 h after IM
Store dry powder at 20-25 C; reconstituted solution per labeling (refrigerate, use within stated time)
pearls: Antipseudomonal fourth-generation cephalosporin; good gram-negative and gram-positive coverage
Cefepime-induced neurotoxicity is underrecognized - suspect in renal impairment with altered mental status, myoclonus, or seizures
Pair with metronidazole for intra-abdominal infections (limited anaerobic coverage)
EEG may show nonconvulsive status epilepticus in unexplained encephalopathy
missed: Doses are scheduled by clinical staff; a delayed dose should be given as soon as possible while maintaining the prescribed interval. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose, especially with renal impairment, causes neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus). Discontinue the drug, provide supportive care and anticonvulsants as needed; hemodialysis can remove cefepime and may be used to manage accumulation.
